subject: Axion Tech connector outage / on-call escalation and SLA coordination
messages:
From: Maya Gupta <maya@axiontech.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Support Ops <support@axiontech.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: customer connector failing — SLA window breached

Priyom / Redwood team,

We started seeing errors in the Axion->Redwood connector at ~08:05 PT this morning. Multiple customers are reporting timeouts and partial responses; our monitoring shows token-level latency exceeding the SLAs for three customer accounts. This is impacting our May onboarding wave.

Attached is a short sample of the error stream (axion-error-log-0501.txt). Can you confirm receipt and advise on the expected time to mitigation? We have an internal SLA clause that requires acknowledgement within 2 hours for Sev2 incidents.

- Maya
Director, Platform Partnerships
Axion Tech
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Gupta <maya@axiontech.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Support Ops <support@axiontech.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: customer connector failing — SLA window breached

Maya — thanks for flagging and for the log. We received axion-error-log-0501.txt (attached).

Quick plan:
- I’ve escalated this to our on-call infra engineer (Dev Patel) and looped Hannah to coordinate partner comms.
- Dev: can you triage the logs, confirm whether this is a model runtime regression or a request-routing issue, and share ETA for a mitigation patch?
- Maya / Ben: please keep channel updated with any additional customer IDs / timestamps.

We’ll aim to have an initial technical update within 2 hours and a mitigation plan within 6 hours.

If needed, we can put a temporary traffic-split to a slower but stable model variant to reduce error surface while we investigate.

— Priyom
Enterprise Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Maya Gupta <maya@axiontech.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: customer connector failing — SLA window breached

Quick findings from the ingested logs:
- Elevated latencies correspond to a spike in requests with long system prompts that exceed our prefix cache heuristics; this causes repeated KV cache misses and a fallback code path with higher latency.
- I see a small increase in OOM retries on a subset of dedicated instances (node ids: rwd-gpu-12/13).

Immediate actions taken:
- Scoped the requests by client ID and enabled a temporary prefix-cache bypass for the affected customers to prevent cache thrashing (this reduces throughput but improves latency).
- Spun up two extra burst instances in the dedicated pool.
- Pushed a candidate mitigation (hotfix) that changes cache-eviction thresholds; attaching patch: hotfix-patch.diff.

Next steps / ask of Axion: if you can route a small traffic slice to test the mitigation (5%) for 30 minutes and share telemetry, we’ll validate and then roll to 100%.

— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Gupta <maya@axiontech.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Lloyd <ben.lloyd@axiontech.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: customer connector failing — SLA window breached

Thanks Dev. Maya / Ben — following our internal test results (Dev’s candidate patch), here’s a concise Mutual Action Plan I’d like to propose (attaching mutual-action-plan.xlsx):

- Today (05/03): 5% traffic canary for 30 minutes starting 16:00 PT. Redwood will monitor latency, error rate, and token cost.
- 05/04: Expand to 25% for 2 hours pending green signals.
- 05/05: Full roll if no regressions.
- Escalation policy: if error rate >1.5% or p95 latency degrades by >30% vs baseline, Redwood will rollback within 15 minutes and notify Axion execs.

I’ll also open a Zendesk ticket for the incident so we have a traceable timeline: https://redwood.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/7219

Please confirm the canary window and the contact for on-call validation (who on your side will confirm telemetry is OK).

— Hannah
Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Gupta <maya@axiontech.com>, Ben Lloyd <ben.lloyd@axiontech.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Support Ops <support@axiontech.com>
Date: 2026-05-05T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: customer connector failing — SLA window breached

Maya / Ben — thank you for working through this with us. Final status and commitments: 

- Canary run (05/03 16:00 PT) showed p95 latency improvement of ~22% vs the pre-patch baseline and error rate dropped from 2.8% to 0.3% in the test window.
- We expanded to 25% on 05/04 and saw stable metrics. Full roll completed on 05/05 at 03:20 PT.
- Root cause: cache-eviction thresholds not adapting to a sudden shift in long prompts; Dev’s patch adjusts thresholds and adds an instrumentation flag for early detection.

Action items we’ve committed to: 
1) Add an automated guard that will trigger an autoscale + cache-threshold adjustment if median prompt length for a customer increases >2x within a 30-minute window. (Owner: Dev, ETA 2 weeks)
2) Formalize the partner SLA runbook and add explicit on-call steps for partner escalations (Owner: Hannah, ETA 1 week).
3) Share a short postmortem and the mutual-action-plan spreadsheet to your legal/ops stakeholders. (Owner: Priyom, ETA 48 hours)

I’ve attached the shared docs; I’ll follow up with the postmortem and the Doc with on-call contact names. If you want a quick sync, we can hop on a 30m call tomorrow.

Appreciate the partnership and the quick turn.

— Priyom
Enterprise Partnerships, Redwood Inference
